item.title: Insurance firms called on to improve claims handling
item.description: We are helping firms learn from Financial Ombudsman complaints and strengthen their claims handling in line with our existing rules to improve service quality for insurance customers. The report highlights where claims handling can improve and explains the key rules firms need to meet. Building on findings in our 2025 review of home and travel insurance , it calls on insurers to: While 79% of people who make a claim are satisfied with claims handling (PDF) , improvements are needed in consumer understanding and service quality.

item.description: Speech by Sarah Pritchard, deputy chief executive, at TheCityUK National Conference 2026. item.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
item.description: Panics and pile-ons are a familiar pattern in the public markets, with a herd mentality wiping value from companies in an instant. It revealed the limits of public markets in judging its value. This pattern erodes trust in the public markets.

item.title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course
item.description: The next two largest fundraisers on our list for this year are focused on automating more employer tasks. So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. As you can see, it’s a varied list, with a commonly shared theme of bringing more automation to hiring, HR and payroll tasks.

item.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities
item.description: To put this in perspective: If the blue economy were a country, it would be the world’s fifth largest. And as the world turns back to the sea to face increasingly critical challenges, from geopolitical instability to rising energy prices and climate resilience, the blue economy is set to become even more central. The “blue economy,” which encompasses industries built around oceans and coasts — from shipping and fisheries to offshore energy and marine biotechnology — is one of the largest, yet least visible, engines of the global economy.

item.title: Allied World raises target to $375m for 2001 CAT Re 2026-1 catastrophe bond
item.description: Now, we’re told that Allied World is looking for even more protection from its latest catastrophe bond, with the target size raised to now seek $375 million of retrocession from the issuance of three tranches of 2001 CAT Re 2026-1 notes. Allied World Assurance Company (AWAC) is aiming to upsize its new catastrophe bond sponsorship to provide $375 million of protection, while also targeting strong execution as the price guidance has been lowered for all three tranches of 2001 CAT Re Ltd. Allied World Assurance Company (AWAC), the global insurance and reinsurance company that is part of the Fairfax Financial group, returned to the catastrophe bond market for a renewal and expansion of its protection earlier this month.

item.title: Capital markets signal resilience for Lloyd’s despite rate softening narratives: ICMR
item.description: As rate softening continues to take shape across the Lloyd’s market, Insurance Capital Markets Research (ICMR) has pointed to the capital markets as proof that investors see a more resilient outlook and considerable upside potential ahead. Moreover, Insurance Capital Markets Research also emphasises that while direct data on rate softening is too inconsistent and client-specific to measure accurately, it instead relies on the broader, aggregate perspective of the capital markets to gauge its overall impact. However, while the new launches demonstrate “sustained capital appetite”, ICMR stressed that they could potentially add underwriting capacity into classes already facing downward rate pressure, widening the gap between top-quartile cycle managers and those chasing volume.

item.title: AXA XL hires Subramanian to Alternative Capital team in London
item.description: AXA XL has hired Murali Subramanian as a quantitative specialist for its Alternative Capital team in London, where he will focus on developing insurance-linked securities and capital solutions across the firm’s broad portfolio of risks. At AXA XL, Subramanian has taken on the London-based position of Quantitative Specialist, Investor Relations, focused on ILS and Alternative Capital Solutions. “Pleased to share that I have joined AXA XL’s Alternative Capital team in London.

item.title: Frequent acquirers better placed to achieve insurance M&A goals: Oxbow Partners and InsurTech NY
item.description: Insurance companies with established acquisition programmes may be more successful at securing the anticipated benefits of mergers and acquisitions (M&A), according to a joint study by Oxbow Partners, a specialist insurance management consultancy, and InsurTech NY, an organisation supporting connections between insurers, technology businesses and investors. Oxbow Partners and InsurTech NY assessed 333 publicly listed insurance carriers and gathered perspectives from industry executives and transaction specialists with experience of significant insurance deals. Oxbow Partners and InsurTech NY suggest that decisions concerning how businesses will operate together should form part of the initial assessment of a potential acquisition.

item.title: Tokio Marine’s international insurance profit rises 13% to JPY 266.8bn in Q2’26
item.description: Tokio Marine’s international business has reported a total insurance profit of JPY 266.8 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 12.7% from JPY 236.8 billion in the same period a year earlier. The increase in profit was driven by strong underwriting, primarily in North America, which generated an insurance profit of JPY 230.9 billion, a 20.2% increase from JPY 192 billion a year earlier. LATAM also recorded significant growth, with insurance profit increasing 99.4% to JPY 21.5 billion from JPY 10.7 billion.

item.title: Canopius Reinsurance adopts ACORD Solutions Group’s ADEPT Platform in Bermuda
item.description: Canopius Reinsurance Limited has introduced the ADEPT digital data exchange platform in Bermuda to manage the transfer of accounting, claims and financial settlement information with its broker partners, according to ACORD Solutions Group, a provider of digital data exchange and technology solutions for the global insurance industry. We are pleased to support the continued rollout of ADEPT in Bermuda.” The adoption extends the use of ACORD Solutions Group’s ADEPT technology in Bermuda, with Canopius Reinsurance Limited planning to incorporate additional brokers into the platform as part of its ongoing digital data exchange arrangements. Bringing data and query capabilities together on one platform supports more efficient processing of transactions and settlements in Bermuda and provides a scalable approach as we extend its use to additional brokers.” ACORD Solutions Group said the implementation represents another deployment of its technology within Bermuda’s insurance and reinsurance sector, where digital data exchange is being used to support the administration of accounting, claims and settlement activities.

item.title: Dutch Privacy Watchdog Advises Consumers Not to Purchase Smart Glasses
item.description: The Netherlands’ privacy watchdog AP on Thursday advised consumers not to purchase smart glasses, or AI-powered glasses with cameras, saying they are unsafe for both users and bystanders, after studying six types available on the Dutch market. Dutch consumer and rights groups sued Meta in October, alleging its glasses violate privacy laws, with a preliminary hearing scheduled for Nov. Also in October, Dutch retail chain Hans Anders suspended sales of Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses in the Netherlands and Belgium, in one of the first such moves by a retailer.

item.title: With Rates on the Level, ‘Stable’ Personal Lines Move to Growth: AM Best
item.description: personal lines insurers is shifting from a focus on rate increases toward affordability, underwriting transparency, and oversight of artificial intelligence and predictive modeling, according to AM Best. personal lines, but competition for profitable growth could be challenging for some carriers now that a period with a focus on rate adequacy has eased. “While the profitability in the personal lines segment has rebounded, a sense of heightened competition on pricing will test whether insurers can sustain those gains,” said Chris Draghi, director, AM Best.

item.title: Iran Intensifies Hormuz Tanker Attacks Just as Oil Prices Slide
item.description: Iran’s attacks on oil tankers crossing the crucial Strait of Hormuz are getting more intense, just as prices have tumbled due to a flood of supply from the Middle East. “Oil is going out, but being certain about the volumes is complicated by the attacks and the secrecy.” Another issue is that while oil is flowing through Hormuz, more and more vessels will be needed as some are lost to attacks, he said. One senior Saudi shipping official said at a conference last week that the kingdom has no choice but to continue shipping oil through Hormuz, despite the attacks.

item.title: $3m financing backs launch of AI-enabled E&S MGA Alpine Specialty
item.description: Alpine Specialty, a newly formed managing general agent (MGA) based in Raleigh, North Carolina, has launched with its own agentic AI underwriting software and closed a $3m initial financing. "I'm grateful for the support of investors I've known and respected for many years, including former coworkers, industry colleagues, and mentors," said Connor Leonard, Founder and CEO of Alpine Specialty. "By combining experienced underwriting judgment with technology built specifically for our business, we can deliver faster, more efficient responses to wholesale brokers while maintaining the discipline and rigor that sound underwriting requires," said Allen Clyborne, Chief Underwriting Officer of Alpine Specialty.

item.title: Apis Partners takes minority stake in specialty MGA Alchemy Underwriting
item.description: Apis Partners has agreed to make a minority investment in Alchemy Underwriting, a London-based specialty insurance MGA, through its Apis Global Growth Fund III. Andrew Wallas, Chairman of Alchemy Underwriting, said: "We have experienced a strong sense of alignment, collaboration and partnership with Apis and look forward to growing the business as partners." Matteo Stefanel, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Apis Partners, said: "London is the most important specialty insurance market in the world, which rewards underwriters who deliver consistent results. Alchemy combines a world-class team with a disciplined approach to underwriting, and its MGA model provides a scalable platform which is highly attractive to underwriting talent." Apis Partners is a London-headquartered private equity firm focused on financial infrastructure and technology, with $2.3bn in assets managed or advised.

item.title: Boost Insurance approved as Lloyd’s coverholder and adds nine reinsurers to its panel
item.description: The post Boost Insurance approved as Lloyd’s coverholder and adds nine reinsurers to its panel appeared first on Insurtech Insights . (Boost), the New York-based full-stack specialty MGA platform, has been approved as a Lloyd’s coverholder and has added nine new global capacity partners to its reinsurance panel. "The Lloyd’s Coverholder designation and this expanded reinsurance panel represent years of platform investment coming together in a way that meaningfully changes what we can do for program partners," said Alex Maffeo, CEO & Founder of Boost.

item.title: Adam Riese takes over Neodigital portfolio
item.description: Adam Riese , the digital brand of Württembergische Versicherung, has completed the takeover of Neodigital Versicherung AG’s property, liability and accident insurance portfolio following all required approvals. The portfolios of both Neodigital and Adam Riese will be administered on Neodigital’s technology, including policy and claims processing. The transfer covers more than 400,000 customers and takes effect retroactively to January 1, 2026.

item.title: How AI can Help Carriers Become the Partner Agents Prefer
item.description: Rather than carrier partners handling the routine, agents and carriers can work together in the cases that need interaction, and the relationships become richer. By redesigning distribution workflows around agents’ needs, carriers can simplify operations, strengthen relationships, and position themselves as partners agents prefer to do business with. AI and automation are creating new opportunities for insurance carriers to rethink how they work with agents.

item.title: Protective names legal and digital & AI chiefs
item.description: Protective Life announced that Kurt Meyers will join Protective as EVP, Chief Legal Officer and that Fernando Levy has joined as SVP, Chief Digital & AI Officer, a newly created role. Meyers will succeed Mark Drew as Chief Legal Officer, leading Protective’s legal, compliance and government affairs organization. He will serve as a strategic partner to the CEO, board of directors and leadership team, helping Protective navigate legal, compliance and regulatory matters in support of its business objectives.

item.title: Tesla’s licensed carriers report Q3 2026 results
item.description: Tesla’s three licensed carriers reported their Q3 2026 financial results. Tesla Insurance Company, which offers coverage in California and Illinois, wrote $740.5 million in direct premiums in the first nine months of 2026, up 43% from $517.9 million a year earlier. Tesla Property & Casualty, which offers coverage in CO, MD, FL, MN, OH, TX, IN, TN, and UT, wrote $163.3 million in direct premiums in the first nine months of 2026, up 8% from $151.7 million a year earlier.

item.title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut
item.description: Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq tomorrow with a growth story that’s unlike any I’ve seen in close to three decades working in Silicon Valley: The company says revenue reached $17 billion in Q3, less than four years after Claude launched with zero. The San Francisco-based company also presents a stark contrast to the more common theme in recent years of venture-backed companies staying private longer: Anthropic is less than six years old as it goes public in a potentially record-setting listing. Those metrics are impressive, but there are other numbers in its S-1 I keep circling, too, like the nearly $900 billion in compute purchase and lease commitments.

item.title: Anthropic Prices IPO Shares At $83, Above Range
item.description: Anthropic priced shares for its upcoming stock market debut at $83 on Wednesday afternoon, solidly above the expected range of $70 to $78 laid out in its IPO filing, CNBC, Reuters and the Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. For the IPO portion of its fundraise, Anthropic plans to sell just over 800 million shares, bringing in about $66.4 billion. The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.

item.title: Morningstar DBRS calls for federal insurance backstop to strengthen Canada’s quake resilience
item.description: A government-supported insurance backstop would strengthen financial resilience and help support the stability of credit ratings.” According to Morningstar DBRS, introducing a federal insurance backstop could provide an additional layer of financial protection against extreme earthquake losses, complementing insurers’ existing capital and risk management arrangements. Morningstar DBRS, a global credit rating agency, has raised concerns over the potential impact of a severe earthquake on Canada’s insurance market, identifying federal government involvement in catastrophe insurance as a possible means of limiting financial losses and protecting the sector from widespread disruption. Morningstar DBRS explained that the country’s existing approach depends largely on commercial insurance arrangements and the Disaster Financial Assistance Arrangements (DFAA) programme, through which the federal government supports provincial and territorial disaster recovery efforts.

item.title: Cal-Maine Foods Shuts Production at Florida Facility Due to Bird Flu
item.description: Cal-Maine Foods said on Wednesday it would cull about 1.8 million birds after avian influenza was detected at one of its Florida facilities, forcing the US egg producer to temporarily halt production at the site. The company said it has suspended production at the facility while following US Department of Agriculture protocols, and will cull 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets, representing 2.7% of its flock. The highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly called bird flu, has led to the culling of hundreds of millions of birds over the past few years, disrupting food supplies and driving up prices, though human infections remain rare.

item.title: Florida Mayor Declares Emergency as More Flooding Expected on East Coast
item.description: The mayor of Hollywood, Florida, declared a state of emergency as southeast parts of the state endured a new round of flooding after more than a foot of rain fell in just a few hours. “As low pressure develops and strengthens near the coast, winds from the east and northeast will increase.” The flooding in southeast Florida this week followed a previous round of unusually heavy rains, with floodwaters so high that it forced the temporary closure of a 90-bed rehabilitation hospital in Melbourne, Florida, last week, and flooded a number of homes and businesses. And more trouble may be on the way for the Southeast: AccuWeather meteorologists warned that the tropical system that triggered much of the deluge this week could bring more heavy rains and flooding to Florida and the Carolinas, and then into New York and New England by early next.

item.title: Strike Risk Grows at Busiest US Ports as Contract Talks Stall
item.description: Contract negotiations between security workers at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach and their employers have stalled, setting up a “real potential” for a strike starting on Saturday that could impact operations, according to the group representing terminal operators and ocean carriers. Related: Employers, Watchmen at California Ports Extend Contract Talks The previous labor contract expired in July 2025, and the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service has been assisting with negotiations between the ILWU’s Local 26, which represents about 250 security workers, and the employers. on Saturday, November 21, setting up the real potential for a strike at the nation’s busiest port complex,” PMA said Wednesday.

item.title: Why Insurers' Internal Software Builds Never Finish
item.description: Internal software builds at insurers routinely stretch past two years and $30 million because of a structural misunderstanding. This year I spoke with several people in insurance and insurtech whose internal software builds started in 2025. It found that purchased tools and partnerships succeeded about 67% of the time, and internal builds succeeded one-third as often.

item.title: The Claim Runs on the Data Captured First
item.description: The capture from the first visit has become the foundation the rest of the claim is built on, and increasingly the foundation that automation and artificial intelligence are built on, too. It is whether the capture produced data the rest of the claim can actually use. If it was not captured on the first visit, it is gone for good.

item.title: Allianz Life-backed Transparency Analytics discloses $3.4 million raise
item.description: Transparency Analytics , a New York-based credit ratings and analytics company backed by Allianz Life Ventures, reported selling $3.42 million in equity to five investors in a November 16 SEC filing. Allianz Life Ventures participated in the company’s December 2025 round, which was led by Deciens Capital and also included Mouro Capital, FJ Labs, SUM Ventures and Core Innovation Capital. Transparency Analytics assesses the creditworthiness of corporate borrowers and offers an automated portal that generates a preliminary rating based on the proposed terms of a debt instrument.

item.title: EightbyZero raises $3 million
item.description: Montréal-based EightByZero raised $3 million in seed funding led by Diagram, with participation from Canada Life as a strategic investor. EightbyZero connects insurers, third-party administrators, employers, and HR systems through APIs and file transfers. The insurance technology startup is also working with Munich Re Life US to help its group and disability insurance clients connect to employer data.

item.title: Intact expands global insurance network
item.description: Intact Insurance has added Guardian Group and Ceylinco Insurance to its global network, extending its multinational insurance capabilities from more than 150 countries and territories to more than 170. Guardian Group expands Intact’s Caribbean footprint to markets including Aruba, Barbados, Belize, Curaçao, and the British Virgin Islands, complementing existing relationships in Trinidad and the Bahamas. Ceylinco Insurance brings the Maldives into the network.

item.title: Helping more people break the cycle of persistent credit card debt
item.description: We found that the proportion of credit card accounts in persistent debt fell by more than half between 2018 and early 2023, from 7% to 3%. Credit cards are a useful financial tool for many – offering flexibility and helping people manage spending and cash flow. In the 6 months after receiving their first persistent debt letter, over half of these customers raised their average repayments, around two-thirds reduced their average debt, and a majority reduced the proportion of their available credit they were using.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: Investors Turn Up The Volume On Voice AI
item.description: Voice AI — technology that lets computers understand and generate human speech — is drawing billions of dollars from investors as startups find more ways to put it to work. The broad trend: Investors are putting more money into fewer startups developing or offering voice AI technology and are backing everything from automated customer service to speech generation and content creation. Overall, deal volume is on track to fall for a second consecutive year — pointing to a market where investors are putting more money into fewer companies.

item.title: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough
item.description: Through the early part of the generative AI boom, growth was steep enough that few people pressed the point. ARR became standard in the mid- to late-2000s, when software moved from licence fees to recurring subscriptions. An annualized figure blends revenue a customer has committed to with revenue that depends on what they use next month.

item.title: Texas Farm Bureau secures $400m Fish Pond Re 2026-1 cat bond at reduced pricing
item.description: Texas Farm Bureau Insurance Companies has now successfully priced and finalised its second catastrophe bond sponsorship, securing the 60% upsized $400 million of named storm reinsurance from this Fish Pond Re Ltd. Initially, the Texas Farm Bureau Insurance Companies was seeking $250 million of named storm reinsurance, from this new Series 2026-1 issuance of notes by Fish Pond Re . You can read all about Texas Farm Bureau Insurance’s second catastrophe bond, this Fish Pond Re Ltd.

item.title: IFSCA working group finalises ILS and SPI regulatory recommendations for India
item.description: A working group convened by India’s International Financial Services Centre Authority (IFSCA) to look at how insurance-linked securities (ILS) could be brought under the country’s insurance regulatory regime has finalised its recommendations, calling for laws to be amended to support a special purpose insurer (SPI) structure. Alongside regulatory moves to enable ILS to be transacted in India’s GIFT City under IFSCA regulatory oversight, the working group also calls for the parallel establishment of other expert service providers and capabilities, to enable modelling, actuarial, insurance management and oversight of ILS transactions to be robust and proportionate. The working group recommends the establishment of a regulatory framework, through amendments to the existing insurance code, that would allow for an ILS structure to be used for catastrophe bonds, reinsurance sidecars and other alternative risk transfer use-cases.

item.title: SafePoint now targeting upsized $125m Nature Coast Re 2026-4 catastrophe bond
item.description: SafePoint Insurance Company is looking to upsize its fourth catastrophe bond sponsorship so far in 2026, with the target now to secure $125 million of reinsurance protection to add to its recently priced indemnity deal, through this Nature Coast Re Ltd. Earlier this month, SafePoint priced and secured its largest catastrophe bond ever, with the $650 million Nature Coast Re Ltd. These Nature Coast Re 2026-4 cat bond notes will provide protection to SafePoint Insurance Company itself and the two reciprocal exchanges that the company operates: the Louisiana focused Cajun Underwriters Reciprocal Exchange entity, and the Florida homeowner and business owner focused Manatee Insurance Exchange.

item.title: Gallagher Re adds Chris McNamara as MD, Natural Resources
item.description: Gallagher Re, an international reinsurance broking and advisory business, has hired Chris McNamara from broking group Marsh to serve as Managing Director, Natural Resources, effective immediately. In his new role, McNamara will work alongside Gallagher Re’s existing facultative leadership team, focus on further developing the natural resources business, and support cedants with complex risk transfer needs across the oil & gas, power, and renewable energy sectors. Most recently, McNamara served at Marsh as Managing Director and has over 35 years of facultative reinsurance experience.

item.title: Aurora eyes growth with IA Capital investment
item.description: Aurora, the managing general agent (MGA) and algorithmic underwriting-as-a-service business, has secured investment from IA Capital Group to drive its next phase of growth, led by Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Bijal Patel. Aligning with its long-term strategy, Rick Viton, Partner at IA Capital Group, and James Orchard, CEO of QBE Ventures, have been appointed to Aurora’s board. “This investment allows us to take the next step: re-platforming Aurora as AI-native, launching products faster and scaling what we’ve built across more products and insurers.

item.title: Eight by Zero secures $3m seed round to streamline carrier-employer data connectivity
item.description: Already deployed with several carriers across North America, the platform uses artificial intelligence (AI) to support the setup and continued maintenance once a connection is live “Carriers have rebuilt the same integration for every employer they onboard,” said Sam Kasle, Co-Founder and CEO of Eight by Zero. “The capabilities developed by Eight by Zero will further accelerate investments we’re making in technology to simplify how data is connected across benefits and insurance, helping reduce integration complexity for employers and carriers.” (8/0), a universal interoperability platform for insurance, has closed a $3 million seed funding round, led by Montreal-based venture studio Diagram, with participation from Canada Life.

item.description: A broad group of organizations, including insurance industry trade associations, are pushing Congress to pass the Fix Our Forests Act before the end of 2026. “Congress should act now to advance proven mitigation solutions that help protect lives, property, and the long-term affordability and availability of insurance.” The Fix Our Forests Act hasn’t seen any action in more than a year, when a version ( S. From 2007 through 2026, the US experienced 26 billion-dollar wildfires.

item.title: Australia’s Gender Pay Gap Declines to Lowest on Record
item.description: Australia’s national gender pay gap has fallen below 20% for the first time, the latest Workplace Gender Equality Agency snapshot shows. The national gender pay gap was 19.7%, meaning women earn an average of about A$27,400 ($18,500) less than men each year, WGEA said, citing data from the 2025-26 financial year. The small decline in the gap from last year came as women were less over-represented in the lowest pay bracket, more women worked full-time and in management roles, and there was stronger earnings growth for women in some industries, including health care and retail trade, WGEA reported.

item.title: Florida’s Stormwater Ponds Become Floating Solar Farms as Costs Fall and Demand Rises
item.description: Floating photovoltaics — solar panels mounted on buoyant structures anchored in reservoirs and ponds — have become less expensive since the technology emerged two decades ago. While the United States has been slow to adopt the technology, Florida’s geography, climate and development history make it particularly well suited for floating solar projects to address growing electricity demand . Of the tens of thousands of retention ponds designed to collect runoff during Florida’s frequent downpours, some are also being used to generate solar power, expanding sustainable energy production in the Sunshine State.

item.title: Columbia Insurance signs five-year partnership for Kalepa’s underwriting AI
item.description: The post Columbia Insurance signs five-year partnership for Kalepa’s underwriting AI appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Columbia Insurance has selected Kalepa's Professional Grade AI platform for its underwriting operations under a five-year partnership, Kalepa announced on 17 November. Todd Ruthruff, President and Chief Executive Officer of Columbia Insurance, said: "We committed to a five-year partnership with Kalepa because we see this as a foundational investment in how our underwriters will work and how we will build for the future." Daniel Hillman, Chief Operating Officer and Co-Founder of Kalepa, said: "Professional Grade AI makes it possible to systematically allocate work between AI and human expertise, strengthening risk selection and underwriting discipline while creating the operating leverage required for profitable growth." Founded in 1889, Columbia Insurance provides property and casualty insurance for small and mid-sized businesses across 14 states.
